title: Stop the log tailer without paging anyone

blocks.text: The edge proxies stream their access logs to a collector, and the collector runs one `LogTailer` per proxy. Each tailer reads its proxy's socket on a thread of its own. When a proxy is retired, the collector calls `stop()` on its tailer, and that call never returns: the collector's admin thread hangs until someone restarts it.
Reading already works. Finish the two `TODO`s in `src/main/java/practice/LogTailer.java`:

items: `stop()`: end the tailer and wait for its thread;
`readFailed(...)`: what happens when a read throws.

blocks.text: When you're done, `stop()` returns even when the proxy has gone quiet, retiring a proxy doesn't page on-call, and a connection that really breaks still does. About six lines in total.
The tests hand the tailer a stream that behaves like a socket's on a platform thread.

cases.says: every line is handed on in order until the remote side ends the stream, and stop() then returns
stop() returns while the reader is waiting for a line that may never come
stopping the tailer is not reported as a broken stream
a stream that really breaks is still reported

origin.section: Classic I/O Doesn't Hear an Interrupt: Close What It Waits On

concepts: A platform thread blocked in classic socket I/O is not woken by an interrupt; closing what it waits on frees it, and that exception means a stop, not a failure.
